subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users versus keep only in logs or metadata?
rationale: Current code already has provider/model, token-budget, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session/channel identifiers and exact counts changes privacy, support, and user-facing recovery behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
options.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

options.title: Keep Details Operator-Only
options.body: Leave chat copy generic and document where operators can inspect logs, status, or context-budget metadata for the detailed facts.

options.title: Defer To Broader Visibility Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until broader context-pressure warnings, compaction notices, and overflow messages share one product policy.

recommendation.title: Show Redacted Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.
